claim: Pre-registered cohort of the Fable-versus-swarm comparison. Arm F outcomes are what the receipts on disk say; no verifier was re-run to fill this file. The instructions of the agentic Fable sessions are not in the repository, so stratum D is an outcome comparison, not a paired one.

protocol.sha256_basis: sha256 of the file bytes with CRLF folded to LF

strata.D: prompts with a completed expensive-model derivation run (Fable) in dag/results
strata.P: prompts with expensive-model ladder attempts (Opus, Fable) on a recorded packet
strata.C: matched never-run controls (swarm only; yield and abstention rates, no parity claim)

items.note: The model never reads the prompt file; both arms receive the packet compiled from the operad collection (llm_ladder/packets.py). The packet identity is packet_bytes_sha256, recorded at run time.

runs.model_basis: Co-Authored-By trailer on the commit that added the folder: Fable 5.1
Co-Authored-By trailer on the commit that added the folder: Fable 5.1

cost.estimate_method: LOWER BOUND ONLY. committed authored bytes of the unrecorded runs (Lean sources, run notes, twins and their tests; no receipts, no binaries) / 3.5 bytes per token x USD 50 per million output tokens (claude-fable-5-1 list price in llm_ladder/config.py). It omits thinking, tool calls, every re-read of context, repairs and abandoned attempts, so the true cost is higher. The user may supply the real session cost in cost_overrides.json (see PROTOCOL.md 6.4).

no_expensive_model_provenance.reason: The commit has no Co-Authored-By model trailer and the folder carries no model field, or the folder text names Codex (the batch runs of 2026-10-19..20). Such runs may have been made by a large model but cannot be shown to be; they are not Arm F.

sonnet_reference_only.reason: Sonnet 5.5 is not in the expensive set (list price 2/10 USD per million tokens against 10/50 for Fable). The 26 batch-1 staged runs (positions 152-177) are listed for context only.

opus_runs.reason: No completed Opus run folder exists other than the ladder attempts of stratum P. Opus commits are tooling, migration and DAG work, and Opus sub-agents wrote the Python and Rust twins inside Fable sessions (named in validation.json); neither is a prompt run.
